clue.text: Time to joke in greater measure — it calls for continuing interest

indicators.note: in tells us the time-and-joke pieces sit inside the word for a greater measure

parts.note: a greater measure is more
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone recommends making a joke last longer, as if humour needed sustained attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan requires the borrower to keep paying interest over many years, so it calls for continuing interest.

clue.text: Contemplate taking the mickey — there's nothing to lose

indicators.note: to lose says a piece must be dropped from the cartoon character's name

parts.note: Mickey is the cartoon mouse, so mickey gives mouse
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A thinker reflects on mockery and concludes there is nothing to be lost by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the mickey' looks like the idiom for mocking; here it simply means take the word suggested by Mickey (Mouse).
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or think deeply, a direct synonym for contemplate.

clue.text: Beached prince finds the reason

parts.note: a rana is a Hindu prince or rajah in India and Nepal
the ground for something is the reason for it

explanation.surface: A prince discovers why something happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has run onto the shore and stuck there has been beached.

clue.text: See 3
Power failure in the family?

parts.note: read the first words as a break in electricity production, then as the divide in outlook between parents and children

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the difference in attitudes and values between older and younger family members.

clue.text: Art collection on board — for America probably

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the gallery sits within the ship's letters

parts.note: a board suggests a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Paintings are being shipped across the Atlantic to the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art collection' looks like a list of paintings, but it names a specific London gallery; 'board' is the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is often called simply the States, so America is a probable example.

clue.text: It's found in church building patterns

indicators.note: building suggests constructing something new out of the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A church's architecture shows decorative patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-arm of a cruciform church is one of the parts of its architecture.

clue.text: They said: "Try the sweet" — I did and dance for joy

indicators.note: They said tells us the first word is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: try said aloud gives the same sound as tri
pud is short for pudding, the sweet course
in context I did means I ate it, so did gives ate

explanation.surface: Diners urged someone to taste the dessert; they did, and were delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripudiate is a rare word meaning to dance or leap for joy, from Latin tripudium.

clue.text: Constructive way to feel sets me up

indicators.note: up here means stirred or disturbed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a positive feeling puts them in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect for oneself is a positive, constructive frame of mind.

clue.text: Drink to a detractor of the gutter press?

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, typical of the gutter press
someone who does another down is a downer or detractor

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to someone who criticises the tabloids.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset.

clue.text: Abandon garment? Not entirely — turn it over to him

indicators.note: turn it over says the letters are flipped about and rearranged
not entirely means the word is cut short of its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone discards a piece of clothing and hands it to the scrap collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the T of GARMENT; 'turn it over' rearranges ABANDON plus GARMEN. A rag-and-bone man was a British street trader who collected old clothes and scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: The collector of unwanted clothes is the man the garment would be handed to.

clue.text: Spirit shown by one in a brief relation

indicators.note: in places the number one inside the shortened word
brief tells us the word is cut short, keeping its first three letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spirit appears through a family member's short visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Nasty English rugger scrimmage may provoke a dissenting signal

indicators.note: a scrimmage is a confused scrum, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rough English rugby scrum might provoke an obscene hand sign.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugger is British slang for rugby union football.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude hand sign of protest is a dissenting signal.

clue.text: Help people to see how a contemptuous indifference came about

indicators.note: came about suggests one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a slight is a snub, a show of contemptuous indifference

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a snub arose.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine a lamp for others is to help them see.

clue.text: Tale told about a fellow may be excused

indicators.note: about tells us the story word goes round the fellow

parts.note: a parable is a tale with a moral
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A story told about someone may get them off the hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgivable is a fault that may be excused.

clue.text: Obtain a higher degree in theatre studies

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following word

explanation.surface: A student earns a postgraduate qualification in drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Higher degree' suggests an academic qualification; it is a higher temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat up is to reach a higher temperature, measured in degrees.

clue.text: Position of weasel, first to last?

definitions.text: Position of weasel, first to last?

parts.words: Position of weasel, first to last?
parts.note: split weasel as W then easel, read easel as a support and W as a compass direction, then move the first piece to the end

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where a weasel stands in a ranking from first to last.
explanation.definitionFit: A point of view is a position from which things are considered.

clue.text: What bishop has the right to precede?

definitions.text: What bishop has the right to precede?

parts.words: What bishop has the right to precede?
parts.note: an Anglican bishop is styled Right followed by the title of clergy, so that title is what Right precedes

explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is addressed as 'the Right Reverend'.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtesy title of clergy follows Right in a bishop's formal style.

clue.text: Parliamentarian, a fair speaker?

parts.note: a well-known Conservative MP whose surname is also the Devon village of the folk song about a fair

explanation.walkthrough: Ann Widdecombe was an outspoken Conservative MP; 'Widdecombe Fair' is a traditional English folk song about a Devon fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The MP Ann Widdecombe shares her name with the village famous for its fair.

clue.text: Stop in Tours

parts.note: Tours is a French city, so this asks for the French command to stop

clue.text: Toffs driving from the airport?

parts.note: upper-class people who have just touched down by plane

explanation.walkthrough: Toffs is British slang for upper-class people; the gentry who own estates are 'landed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The estate-owning upper class are known as the landed gentry.

explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning dressed.

clue.text: Roof support starts blowing in the wind

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the strong wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: starts picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A roof's framework begins to give way in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable is the triangular end wall that carries the ridge of a pitched roof.

clue.text: Procure plate carrying bird, which is a bloomer

parts.note: to pimp is to procure

indicators.note: carrying means the plate abbreviation holds the bird inside it

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for plate
the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: A dish with a bird painted on it is obtained, then found to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small flowering plant, so it blooms.

clue.text: Go without an object — it's in fashion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a go is a try
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone does without things, which happens to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, in fashion.

clue.text: Me and my girl in the finish got engaged

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces sit inside the word for the finish

parts.note: the end is the finish
taken as written
she stands for a girl

explanation.surface: A suitor says that he and his girlfriend finally became engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got engaged' suggests marriage; it means caught up, as in a mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enmeshed is to be entangled or caught up, engaged like interlocking parts.
